approach: Add `check_defined_terms(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs as one `step!` in `refusing_check`, after `check_environment_reach` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. It returns Ok for a reading with no capability, a question or no deliverable, as `check_outcome_state` does (reading.rs:3681). Otherwise it reduces the request to plain prose and finds the whole words ladder, rung, tier and layer (plural and possessive too). It refuses when a used term has no `Term <word>:` assumption. Plain prose leaves out: (1) hestia's generated root-cause lines, skipped by exact shape and anchor sentence; (2) the text `work_decisions::approve_request` generates (the 'Rung of the requirements ladder: ' line, the 'Proposal: ... (key ... queued at ...' line, and everything from the '## Source' line on), skipped only when the anchor sentence 'A person approved this proposal from the steward role.' is present; (3) quoted spans; (4) parenthesised example lists; (5) code-like tokens containing `/`, `_` or `::`. Tests build the accepted cases from the real generators (`hestia::root_cause_request`, `work_decisions::approve_request` against a temporary git repository) and pin each generator's line shapes. Revision (round 5): (finding 1) `steward::queued_work` re-checks the stored reading of every proposed request with `check_reading_text`, so a request already read under the old rules whose plain prose uses a term is left out of the drain queue until a person runs `athena go`. This is the existing, documented behavior for any new reading rule (steward.rs:394-399). The plan declares it intended, lists `queued_work` and its caller drain.rs:4202 as dependents, adds a public-path corpus test with a proposed request using 'tier' (left out with no Term line, listed read with one), and states the hold in D164 and the CHANGELOG. (finding 2) When a held send-back reports a measured share, the producer also writes it into the doc comment, CHANGELOG and D164, labelled 'measured by the loop replay', next to the 3% estimate. The declared figure stays 3. (finding 3) D164 names the general fix as follow-up: generators mark cited content with a shared delimiter or constant that reading.rs reads. It is outside this job because hestia.rs and work_decisions.rs are not deliverables.

decisions.choice: Match structural words in plain request prose only: a `plain_request_prose` pre-pass, then the existing `request_words` tokenizer (reading.rs:3507), then whole-word comparison (term, term+s, trailing `'s` stripped first).
decisions.reason: `request_words` splits all text and ignores quoting, and its tokens keep `'` between letters, so "ladder's" would match nothing. The 7bf8 request quotes 'a ladder of requirements' and also uses the term in plain prose, so the pre-pass must drop the first and keep the second. Whole-word tokens keep stepladder, delayer, `ladder.md` and `layer_count` out.

rejected.option: Run `request_words` over the whole request
rejected.why: It ignores quoting, so generated requests that only quote the words would be refused.

rejected.option: Substring match
rejected.why: It refuses stepladder and delayer, which criterion 3 requires to pass.

rejected.option: Treat every parenthesised span as a non-use
rejected.why: It hides real uses such as '(the ladder, which ranks requirements)'.

decisions.choice: Skip hestia's generated lines by exact shape. An `Introspection ` line is skipped only if it also holds ' (job ' and '); prevention it proposed:' (hestia.rs:486-488). `Failure class: `, `Cause: ` and `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: ` lines are skipped only when the request also holds 'The same cause has produced failures in more than one job.' (hestia.rs:467).
decisions.reason: Those lines carry free prose from earlier introspections. Bare prefixes would drop a hand-written 'Introspection of the ladder is needed.' or 'Cause: the ladder has no rung'. The anchor sentence ties the skip to text Athena generated.

rejected.option: Skip any line that starts with introspection, cause: or failure class:
rejected.why: Case-insensitive bare prefixes drop hand-written lines that use a term.

rejected.why: The generated Cause and prevention text is free prose, not quoted.

decisions.choice: Treat `work_decisions::approve_request` text as generated and cited. Anchor: 'A person approved this proposal from the steward role.' (work_decisions.rs:287). When the anchor is present, skip lines starting 'Rung of the requirements ladder: ' (line 290), the 'Proposal: ' line holding ' (key ' and ' queued at ' (line 289), and every line from the first line equal to '## Source' to the end (lines 291-306). The first line (the title) and the sentences between stay plain prose and count.
decisions.reason: `approve_request` is the only Athena generator that writes a structural word as fixed text. Its output reaches the gate through `approve_work` (work_decisions.rs:330-331). The fake reader's default reading has capability change, one deliverable and no Term line, so without the skip every approval is refused and the athena-cli approval tests fail. Content copied from files and jobs is a citation, not the request's own use. The anchor and exact line shapes keep a hand-written 'Rung of the requirements ladder: x' or '## Source' heading counted.

rejected.why: work_decisions.rs is not a listed deliverable, and the line tells the reader the rung of the work. Changing generated text to suit a check moves the fault.

rejected.option: Skip the whole request when it holds the anchor
rejected.why: The title is the steward's own wording and is a real use.

rejected.option: Skip any '## Source' heading and 'Rung of the requirements ladder:' line with no anchor
rejected.why: A hand-written request with those lines would escape the check.

decisions.choice: Quote and parenthesis handling: remove straight and curly double-quoted spans, backtick pairs and single-quoted spans (opener after start/whitespace/`(` and before a letter or digit; closer after a non-space and before a non-alphanumeric; an unclosed opener stays as text). Scan per line. Remove a parenthesised span only if it has two or more commas or opens with e.g., i.e., such as, for example or like. Replace whitespace-delimited tokens containing `/`, `_` or `::` with a space.
decisions.reason: A single-comma parenthetical such as '(the ladder, which ranks requirements)' is a real use and stays counted; '(ladder, layer, tier)' has two commas and is dropped. Per-line scanning means a stray apostrophe cannot swallow the rest of the request.

rejected.option: Drop any parenthesised span that holds a comma
rejected.why: It hides a real use with a single comma.

decisions.choice: A term is defined by an assumption that, trimmed and lowercased, starts `term <word>:` followed by at least 3 words. A trailing `s` or `'s` on the word is dropped when the base is in STRUCTURAL_TERMS. The line may cite the defining file.

decisions.choice: Measurement path (round-5 revision, finding 2). The doc comment, CHANGELOG and D164 declare 'expected 3% of newly refused readings' as an estimate and say the measured share is recorded in the job's replay record at verification. The producer sees a share only in a held send-back (`replay_problem`, run/producer.rs:61-68, 370-399), sent only above declared+5 = 8%. When a send-back arrives, the producer (a) may change only `plain_request_prose`, never STRUCTURAL_TERMS, and (b) writes the measured percentage from the send-back into the check_defined_terms doc comment, the CHANGELOG entry and D164, in a sentence labelled 'measured by the loop replay' beside the 3% estimate. The declared figure in the reading stays 3. No test asserts a measured figure; the tests keep requiring the 'estimate' wording, which stays.
decisions.reason: The send-back text carries the measured percentage, so the producer has the figure in the one case it can know, and criterion 7 asks for it in the docs. At or under 8% no send-back arrives and the figure lives in the replay record, which the doc states.

rejected.option: Report the measured share only in the producer output
rejected.why: Criterion 7 asks for it in the doc comment and D164; the producer output is not read by later readers.

rejected.option: Producer writes a measured figure when at or under 8%
rejected.why: That branch can never run; no figure reaches the producer.

rejected.option: Narrow the word list when over 8%
rejected.why: The brief fixes the list; the choice is the user's.

rejected.option: A test needle for the measured share
rejected.why: The producer cannot know the share in advance, so a test cannot be satisfied reliably.

decisions.choice: Queued requests read before this change (round-5 revision, finding 1). `steward::queued_work` (steward.rs:402-440) re-checks the latest stored reading of each proposed request with `check_reading_text` and leaves the request out when it fails (steward.rs:420-425, doc 394-399). The plan accepts that behavior and does not edit steward.rs: a proposed request whose plain prose uses a term and whose stored reading has no Term line is held out of `athena plan` and the drain (drain.rs:4202) until a person runs `athena go`, which re-reads it with the refusal text and the READING_RULES line. The hold applies equally to the existing text-only rules whenever one is added. A new test in refusal_corpus.rs drives the public `queued_work` with a hand-built `Records` and shows both sides. D164 and the CHANGELOG state the hold.
decisions.reason: The hold is the documented design for a stored reading that fails a reading check, so no new mechanism is needed. A request that is queued but never read, and one approved after this change, are checked at their own first read, so the hold touches only proposals read earlier. Making it visible in D164 and CHANGELOG, with a test, satisfies the finding.

rejected.option: Re-read held proposals automatically or list them as unread
rejected.why: It changes steward.rs and the drain (not deliverables), and spends reader cost on every proposal after each rule change; named as a possible follow-up for the user.

rejected.option: Say nothing and rely on the existing doc
rejected.why: The finding shows no test or note tells anyone that the new check shrinks the queue.

demonstrations.method: Test `defined_terms_refusal_is_declared_intended` in reading.rs, shaped like `outcome_state_refusal_is_declared_intended`. `replay_declaration` on 'expected 3% of newly refused readings' gives Some(3). The doc comment of `check_defined_terms`, CHANGELOG.md and D164 each contain 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.', 'estimate', that ladder and rung are refused until restated, that plain uses of tier (priority tiers) and layer (a caching layer) are refused too, that the 3% covers hand-written requests only, and that the measured share is recorded in the job's replay record at verification. CHANGELOG and D164 also contain 'held until' with 'athena go' for queued requests read before the change (finding 1). D164 also contains 'decide whether to narrow', 'approve_request', 'accept_request', and the follow-up 'shared delimiter' (finding 3). The check_outcome_state doc must contain 'check_defined_terms' and not 'which does not catch them', and keep 'covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs', the three job ids and 'outside the check'. The corpus case `structural-term-priority-tier-is-refused` pins the known false refusal. There is no needle for a measured figure; if a held send-back reports one, the producer adds it as 'measured by the loop replay' to the doc comment, CHANGELOG and D164 and the tests still pass.
demonstrations.observes: The declared figure parses to 3. Each document carries the sentence, the estimate, the false-refusal, scope, generators, recording, held-queue and narrowing statements. The old 'outside any check' wording is gone. The priority-tier and caching-layer requests are refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the doc comment, CHANGELOG or D164 omits the sentence, the limits, the generators list, the recording path, the held-queue note or the narrowing question, the test fails. If the check_outcome_state doc still says the other two jobs are outside any check, the guard fails. If a later change narrowed 'tier' or 'layer', the pinning case fails.

open_questions: User: If the replay at verification records more than 8% of newly refused readings (the declared 3% plus the 5-point margin), should the list drop 'layer' or 'tier', or should the declared share rise through a revised reading? The planner cannot see records/, and the producer can neither run the replay nor change the accepted reading's declared figure. D164 records this as the user's decision.

User: Should hand-written requests that use 'tier' (Athena's priority tiers) or 'layer' (a caching layer) in a plain technical sense, requests about the repo's own ladder and rung, and a steward-written approval title that uses a term, stay refused until the reading restates them with a Term line? This plan says yes and pins it with corpus cases, as the brief fixes the list.

User: Is it acceptable that proposed requests already read under the old rules and using a term in plain prose are held out of the drain queue until a person runs `athena go` (the documented behavior of steward::queued_work for any failing stored reading), or should a follow-up job re-read them unread instead? This plan accepts the hold and records it in D164.
